page.layout: One column of running text; faint marginal marks overprinted at the right edge, beside the lines "Responsum iis" and "trajecerat"; signature at the foot left, catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: bant, & in occasiones erant intenti: quas ex voto nacti bellum ei simul denunciarunt & intulerunt. Occasionum præcipuæ erant hæ. Laborabant ea ætate factionibus civilibus Carthaginienses, & cladem ingentem recens acceperant à Masinisâ rege vicino, & Utica post Carthaginem in istâ Africæ orâ urbs maxima, non longè à Carthagine disjuncta, & iisdem cum ea conditoribus Tyriis orta, eo ipso tempore quo hæc versabant Romani, sua omnia sponte Romanis dediderant. Ob quæ perculsi Carthaginienses missis semel iterumque Romam legatis ad satisfaciendum, si quid ab se desideraretur, senatui se obtulerunt. Responsum iis [illegible, ~6 letters]mum lubricè, deinde ut consulibus, jam Siciliam cum exercitu trajecerat[illegible, ~4 letters] intra dies xxx pueros totius civitatis nobilissimos ccc fidei obsides darent, aliaque quæ imperatori consules essent, facerent, si declinare bellum, & retinere libertatem vellent. Hæc Carthagi-nem perlata in summam mæstitiam conjecere civitatem: sed quoniam urgebat necessitas, & parendi mora noxia esse posse putabatur, postulato duro mos est gestus, pueri etiam ante præsti-tutum diem per legatos eodem ad consules adducti, non sine ingenti dolore & planctu

page.notes: The right-margin marks (small numerals, letters and overprinted fragments such as "ıı", "ɜ", "tur") are unreadable and overlap the text; they are marked illegible rather than guessed. The phrase "Responsum iis ... mum" is partly hidden by these marks, so the missing letters are not reconstructed. The name "Masinisâ" is read with a doubtful mark over the final vowel. A small stray mark at the lower right ("111-") is not transcribed as it is not clearly printed text. The catchword "planctu" is kept at the foot and not repeated in the text.
